In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nursing labour force in Canada has been relatively stable, with a slight decline over the past decade.
the Canadian nursing labour market is driven by hospital demand, and that hospital demand is a major driver of the supply of nurses.
hospital expenditure is the major driver of nurse supply and demand, but the impact is mediated by the labour force participation of those trained in nursing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supply of nurses in Canada is highly elastic with respect to demand, as reflected by hospital expenditures.
hospital expenditures are an important determinant of the supply of nurses in Canada, and this relationship has not been affected by recent changes to the health system.
the nursing labour market is highly responsive to changes in the demand for nursing services, and that the nursing labour force is highly mobile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nurses who were working outside the nursing profession in 2001 were not lost to the profession, and that the nursing supply was not permanently reduced by the 1991-96 recession.
nurses are not simply a labour supply that can be turned on or off at the discretion of the health care system.
policy makers need to consider the impact of hospital expenditures and other demand-side factors on the labour market for nursing.
